newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil barge premiums ease, U.S. arb beckons.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil barge premiums ease, U.S. arb beckons.

text.p: NWE gas oil barge premiums softened slightly and cargo premiums were talked around 50 cents lower on Friday with traders again focusing on a dispute over the delivery of November IPE futures.
Dec IPE benchmark futures firmed $4.25 to $223.25 per tonne, catching up with Brent's rise on colder U.S. weather.
A barge of heating oil refinery grade traded at Dec IPE +$2 for late Nov, some 50 cents lower. Early Dec was Dec IPE +$1.50/ 2.50, also 50 cents off. Low sulphur diesel was Dec IPE +$12/14.
Traders say the IPE play, involving over 600,000 tonnes, still absorbs most barge capacity in the Rotterdam region.

Trading house AIC, the dominant Nov short, said it appeared Cargill, the main long, had not been able to take full delivery in the first of three five-day delivery periods. Cargill said there were some problems but hoped to resolve these.
Heating oil cargoes were discussed unchanged to 50 cents lower at Dec IPE +$5. Low sulphur was offered and bid at Dec IPE +$16/18 into Bordeaux, equivalent to a $1 lower in Rotterdam.
Traders reported fresh French demand for low sulphur diesel and a possibility the arb on Russians to the U.S. was open.
